note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes how a national standard differs from a job specification?
options: A standard is written by the client; a specification is set by the nation
A standard sets general rules; a specification sets this job's needs
A standard is only advice; a specification is the price list for the job
A standard covers safety only; a specification covers the finish only

questions.stem: A contract says that if documents disagree, the specification takes priority over the drawings. The drawing shows 6 mm fillet welds and the specification asks for 8 mm. What should the team do?
options: Weld 6 mm, because the drawing is what the welders work from
Weld 7 mm, halfway between the two, so that both are nearly met
Stop all work until the client signs a brand-new contract
Weld 8 mm, and ask the engineer to correct the drawing

questions.stem: Why is a controlled copy of a specification stamped and numbered, while an uncontrolled copy is not?
options: So the holder is sent each new revision and the old one is withdrawn
So the controlled copy can be lent or sold to other companies
So the uncontrolled copy can be used as long as it is kept clean
So the controlled copy never needs to be checked again

questions.stem: A welder in your team is working from a photocopy of the welding procedure specification (WPS) that he found in a drawer. What should you do first?
options: Let him carry on, since a procedure seldom changes between jobs
Ask him to sign the photocopy so that it becomes a controlled copy
Check its revision against the register and replace it if out of date
Take it away and let him weld from his own experience instead

questions.stem: Why should you read the scope at the start of a standard before using it on a job?
options: To confirm it covers this job's process, materials and type of work
To find out how much the standard cost and where to buy a copy
To learn the names of the committee members who wrote it
To find the drawing numbers and sizes for this particular job

questions.stem: A specification says: "Welders shall be qualified for the position used. Back gouging should be done by air carbon arc." Which part is a firm requirement?
options: Both parts, because everything in a specification must be done
Neither part, unless the client repeats it in a letter
Back gouging by air carbon arc, and by no other method
Welders being qualified for the position they weld in

questions.stem: A specification says: "Undercut shall not exceed 0.5 mm in depth." You measure undercut 0.8 mm deep along 30 mm of a weld. What is the right decision?
options: Accept it, because the undercut is still less than 1 mm deep
Reject that length, mark it, and repair it by an approved method
Accept it, because only a short length of the weld is affected
Grind the whole weld flat so that the undercut can no longer be seen

questions.stem: Why does a specification give acceptance limits as numbers, such as "no single pore larger than 2 mm", rather than "pores shall be small"?
options: So each welder can decide on the day what counts as small
So the client can change the limit after the job is done
So every inspector reaches the same decision by measuring
So the job can be finished without any inspection at all

questions.stem: Steel plate for a job arrives with its certificate from the steel mill. What should be checked between the certificate and the plate itself?
options: The paint colour on the edges and the total weight of the load
The driver's name and the time that the truck was unloaded
The price per tonne and the date on the supplier's invoice
The heat number, grade and size marked on the plate

questions.stem: On a job that needs traceability, why is the heat number copied onto each part cut from a plate?
options: So every part can be linked back to its material certificate
So the part is easier to find on the racks in the store
So the cutter can be paid for each part that he cuts
So the offcuts can be sold as scrap at a better price

questions.stem: A specification calls for S355 steel. The store has S275 plate of the right size. What should you do?
options: Use it, as plate of the same thickness is always strong enough
Use it, but make every weld larger to make up the difference
Hold it back: S275 is weaker, so get S355 or an approved change
Use it, and mark it as S355 so that the inspector will accept it

questions.stem: What does the number 355 in the steel grade S355 tell you?
options: Its carbon content, which is about 0.355%
Its minimum yield strength, about 355 MPa
The largest thickness made, which is 355 mm
Its melting point, which is about 355 °C

questions.stem: A WPS asks for ER70S-6 wire, but the store only has E71T-1 wire of the same size. Why can the team not simply swap them?
options: E71T-1 is flux-cored, so the process would differ from the WPS
E71T-1 is made for aluminium and will not weld carbon steel
ER70S-6 is a stick electrode, so it will not fit a wire feeder
ER70S-6 is for thin sheet, and E71T-1 is for cast iron only

questions.stem: A low-hydrogen electrode data sheet gives a time limit for leaving the electrodes in open air, and a method for re-drying them. Why does this matter?
options: Damp electrodes draw too much current and burn through the plate
Dry air makes the coating fall off before the electrode is used
The coating changes colour, so the inspector rejects the weld
Moisture in the coating adds hydrogen, which can crack the weld

questions.stem: The manual for a new welding machine gives the supply voltage, the fuse or breaker rating and the cable size it needs. Who should connect it to the supply at the Centre?
options: The welding team leader, once he has read the manual
Any trainee, provided the plug fits the nearest socket
A qualified electrician, following the manual and the Centre's rules
The supplier's driver, before he leaves the Centre

questions.stem: A welding machine's rating plate gives its input current (I1max and I1eff). Why does a team leader need these figures?
options: To set the welding current for each size of electrode used
To check the supply and its protection can carry the load
To work out which filter shade the welder should use
To find how long the arc can be held at full current

questions.stem: Why does the open-circuit voltage (U0) shown on a rating plate matter for safety?
options: It is the voltage the machine draws from the mains supply
It is the voltage across the arc when welding at full current
It shows how much power the machine wastes as heat
It is the voltage at the electrode when no arc is struck

questions.stem: A machine is marked IP23, and its manual says not to use it in rain. A job in Port Maria must be done outdoors in the rainy season. What should you plan?
options: Shelter for the machine and work area, or work on dry days
Use it in the rain, because IP23 means it is fully waterproof
Wrap the machine fully in plastic sheet to keep it dry
Use it in the rain, but turn the current down to lower the risk

questions.stem: A MIG machine's manual gives daily, weekly and six-monthly maintenance tasks. As team leader, how do you make sure they are done?
options: Remind the team once, at the start of the training year
Wait for the machine to fail, then do all of the tasks at once
Put the tasks on a signed checklist and check it each week
Leave a copy of the manual hanging on the side of the machine

questions.stem: A MIG fault-finding chart lists three causes of uneven wire feed: a worn contact tip, a kinked liner and the wrong drive-roll pressure. How should the team use it?
options: Change all three parts at once to save time
Check each cause in turn, testing after each one
Turn the wire speed up until the feed is steady again
Swap the machine for another one and carry on

questions.stem: The parts section of a MIG torch manual shows an exploded view. What is it mainly used for?
options: Showing how the arc and the gas behave during welding
Showing the safe working pressure of the shielding gas
Showing which wire sizes the torch is able to feed
Naming each part, its number and how the parts fit together

questions.stem: A manual gives a tightening torque for the bolts that hold the dies on a bending machine. Why use a torque wrench rather than tightening by feel?
options: Too little lets parts work loose; too much can stretch or snap bolts
A torque wrench is faster, so the job is finished sooner
Tightening by feel is not allowed on any bolt in a workshop
The torque wrench marks each bolt so the inspector can see it

questions.stem: A drawing calls for property class 8.8 bolts. A fitter has some class 4.6 bolts of the same size. What should you decide?
options: Use them, because the size matches the holes in the plate
Use them, with two flat washers under each nut for strength
Do not use them, because class 4.6 bolts are much weaker
Use them, but tighten them harder than a normal bolt

questions.stem: An imported standard gives sizes in inches, but the team's drawings are in millimetres. Which approach best avoids mistakes?
options: Let each member convert the sizes as and when he needs them
Convert once, record both values, and have another person check
Round every size to the nearest 10 mm to keep the numbers simple
Work in inches only and set the millimetre drawings aside

questions.stem: The safety data sheet (SDS) for a degreaser gives a flash point of 23 °C. What does this tell you about using it in a Jamaican workshop?
options: It will freeze if it is stored in a cool place overnight
It is safe near welding because it can only burn above 100 °C
It must be warmed to 23 °C before it will clean properly
It gives off vapour that can catch fire at normal room heat

questions.stem: A two-pack paint data sheet gives a pot life of 4 hours at 25 °C. What does "pot life" mean?
options: How long the mixed paint can be used before it starts to set
How long the unopened tins can be kept in the store
How long the paint takes to become dry to the touch
How many years the paint will protect the steel outdoors

questions.stem: A paint data sheet says: "Do not apply when the steel is less than 3 °C above the dew point." Why?
options: The paint will dry too quickly and crack in the sun
The paint will become too thick to spray evenly
Water may form on the steel, and the paint may not stick
The steel will expand and push the paint off later on

questions.stem: A specification says: "Blast clean to near-white metal and prime the same day." Why must the primer go on the same day?
options: The blast profile wears flat if it is left overnight
Bare blasted steel starts to rust quickly in humid air
The primer will not stick to steel that has cooled down
The blasting grit must be painted over while it is warm

questions.stem: Which change to a qualified welding procedure would normally need a new procedure test?
options: A new helmet for the welder doing the job
A different make of grinding disc for cleaning
Welding in the afternoon instead of the morning
Changing the process, such as from MMAW to FCAW

questions.stem: A welder's qualification record shows he is qualified for plate in the flat and horizontal positions only. The job needs vertical-up welds. What should the team leader do?
options: Give the vertical welds to a welder qualified for them
Let him weld them, since he is a skilled and careful welder
Let him weld them, and ask the inspector to look more closely
Let him practise vertical-up welding on the job itself first

questions.stem: A specification says that 10% of butt welds shall be radiographed (RT). A job has 40 butt welds. What is the least number to be tested?
options: 2 welds
3 welds
4 welds
10 welds

questions.stem: A specification asks for magnetic particle testing (MT) of fillet welds. What can MT find?
options: Porosity deep in the middle of thick aluminium welds
Cracks at or just below the surface of steel welds
The hardness of the weld cap and the parent metal
The chemical make-up of the filler metal used

questions.stem: Why can a dye penetrant test (PT) not find a crack that lies completely inside a weld?
options: The developer hides any crack deeper than 1 mm
The dye only works on stainless steel and aluminium
The dye is washed away before it reaches the crack
The dye can only enter flaws open to the surface

questions.stem: A drawing note says: "Unless stated otherwise, length tolerance ±2 mm." One length is marked 1500 ± 0.5. Which tolerance applies to that length?
options: ±0.5 mm, because a stated tolerance overrides the general note
±2 mm, because the general note applies to every length
±2.5 mm, because the two tolerances are added together
±1.25 mm, the average of the two tolerances given

questions.stem: A trainee asks why he must follow the maker's manual when "everybody does it differently". What is the best reply?
options: Because the manual was written by the most senior welder
Because the manual is a law, and breaking it is a crime
Because the maker tested the method, and safe use depends on it
Because the inspector checks only the manual, not the work

questions.stem: A grinder manual asks for safety glasses. The Centre's rule asks for safety glasses and a face shield. What should the team wear?
options: Safety glasses only, because the maker knows the tool best
Both, because the stricter of the two rules applies
A face shield only, because it covers more of the face
Whatever each person finds more comfortable to wear

questions.stem: Revision C of a specification changes the paint system. Your team has already primed half the gates to revision B. What should you do?
options: Finish all gates to revision B, since the work has started
Strip the primed gates at once, without asking anyone
Paint the rest to revision C and say nothing about the others
Stop painting, tell the supervisor and get a written decision

questions.stem: A wire data sheet gives: 1.0 mm wire on 6 mm plate, 22–24 V and 7–9 m/min; on 10 mm plate, 24–26 V and 9–11 m/min. Which is a sensible starting setting for 6 mm plate?
options: 23 V and 8 m/min
25 V and 10 m/min
22 V and 11 m/min
26 V and 7 m/min

questions.stem: A preheat chart in a procedure shows the preheat rising with plate thickness and with the carbon equivalent of the steel. What does it tell you for thicker plate of the same steel?
options: Less preheat is needed, as thick plate holds heat better
No preheat is needed above a certain thickness
A higher preheat is usually needed
The preheat stays the same whatever the thickness

questions.stem: Why might a Jamaican fabricator work to an American or international welding standard on a hotel project?
options: Because Jamaican standards may not be used on hotels
Because the client's specification names that standard
Because foreign standards are always easier to meet
Because the welders choose the standard they like best

questions.stem: A client asks, a year after handover, which steel grade was used for a handrail. Which records answer this?
options: The time sheets and the delivery driver's log
The quotation and the final invoice for the job
The welding machine's maintenance checklist
The material certificates and traceability record

questions.stem: A standard's definitions section explains "weld size" differently from the way your team uses the term. Which meaning applies on the job?
options: The meaning given in the standard's definitions
The meaning the team has always used in the shop
Whichever of the meanings gives the smaller weld
The meaning in a general English dictionary

questions.stem: A grinding disc label gives a maximum speed of 8 500 rev/min. The grinder's rating plate says 11 000 rev/min. What should you do?
options: Fit it, but press lightly so that the disc is not overloaded
Fit it, and run the grinder for a minute to test it first
Do not fit it: the disc is rated below the grinder's speed
Fit it, as long as the disc is the right diameter

questions.stem: A cylinder label shows a red diamond with a picture of a gas cylinder inside. What hazard does it show?
options: Toxic gas
Gas under pressure
Oxidising gas
Flammable gas

questions.stem: You find that the parts list in a maker's manual gives the wrong part number for a contact tip. What should you do?
options: Cross it out and write the right number without telling anyone
Ignore it, as everyone will soon learn the right number
Throw the manual away and use an internet list instead
Record it, tell the supervisor and report it to the supplier

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A bolt head is marked 8.8. What is the bolt's nominal tensile strength, in MPa?
What word describes an older issue of a document that has been replaced by a newer one?
What is the word for written permission from the client or engineer to accept work or material that does not fully meet the specification?
In a machine's manual, what is the name of the drawing that shows the machine's electrical circuits and how they are connected?
A paint has 50% volume solids. The specification asks for a dry film thickness of 75 µm. What wet film thickness should be applied, in µm? (Wet film = dry film × 100 ÷ volume solids %.)
What is the name of the number stamped or stencilled on steel plate that links it to its mill certificate?
What do the letters IP stand for in an equipment rating such as IP23?
What name is given to the list, near the front of a standard, of other standards that must be used with it?
On a paint data sheet, what is the name for the time you must wait before the next coat can be applied?
What is the name of the section of a manual that lists faults with their likely causes and remedies?
In a European steel grade such as S275, what word does the letter S stand for?
What term is used for the main values in a welding procedure, such as the process or the parent metal, that need a new procedure test if they are changed?
On a welding machine rating plate, what is shown by the symbol X, next to percentages such as 35%, 60% and 100%?
What do the letters MTC stand for, on the paper that comes with a delivery of steel?
What do the letters UT stand for, a test that uses sound waves to find flaws inside a weld?

essays.stem: You are given a specification pack for a steel staircase: the contract specification, the drawings, a WPS, the standard it names and the makers' data sheets. Explain how you would review the pack before the team starts work, and what you would do with any problems you find.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check that I have every document listed and that each is the current revision, by comparing it with the document register. I read the scope of the specification and the standard to confirm they cover this job, its steel and its welding process. Then I read the specification in full and mark the firm ("shall") requirements: materials, weld sizes, acceptance limits, inspection and painting. I compare the drawings, the WPS and the data sheets with the specification and with each other, looking for sizes, grades or consumables that disagree. I also check that our welders' qualifications and our equipment can meet the requirements. Each problem goes on a query log with the documents involved. I do not choose an answer myself: I send the queries in writing to the engineer or client, using the contract's order of priority as a guide, and wait for written answers before that part of the work starts. Finally I brief the team on the key requirements.
markingPoints: Checks every document is present and current against the register
Reads the scope and marks the firm (shall) requirements
Cross-checks the drawings, WPS and data sheets for conflicts
Checks that welder qualifications and equipment can meet the requirements
Logs problems and gets written answers from the engineer or client before that work starts; briefs the team

essays.stem: Explain how a fabrication shop controls its specifications, procedures and manuals so that the team always works from the right issue. Say what you would do if you found an old copy in use.
essays.modelAnswer: Each controlled document has a number, a title and a revision, and is listed in a register that shows the current revision and who holds a copy. Controlled copies are stamped and numbered so that each holder can be sent the next revision. When a new revision is issued, the person in charge of documents sends it to every holder, collects the old copies or marks them superseded, and updates the register. Team members work only from controlled copies, or from the shop's approved screen copy, and check the revision before starting a job. Photocopies and printouts are uncontrolled and are marked that way. If I find an old copy in use, I stop that work, compare the copy with the register and replace it. I then check whether any work was done to the old copy and report it to the supervisor so that a decision can be made. One original of each superseded revision is kept, clearly marked, for the record.
markingPoints: Documents are numbered with revisions and listed in a register
Controlled copies go to named holders; new revisions are sent out and old ones withdrawn or marked superseded
The team works only from controlled or approved copies and checks the revision before work
Old copy found: stop, replace it and check any work done to it
Reports to the supervisor; one marked superseded original is kept for the record

essays.stem: A specification gives these visual acceptance limits for fillet welds: no cracks; undercut not deeper than 0.5 mm; leg length not less than the size on the drawing. Explain how you would inspect a batch of welded brackets against these limits and record the results.
essays.modelAnswer: Before starting I make sure I have the current specification and drawing, good light, a magnifier and gauges in good condition: a fillet weld gauge for leg length and an undercut or bridge cam gauge for depth. The welds are cleaned of slag and spatter so that defects can be seen. I check each weld in the same order every time. First I look for cracks along the toes, the face and the ends; any crack is a reject. Next I measure any undercut at its deepest point and compare it with 0.5 mm. Then I measure both legs at several places along the weld and compare the smallest reading with the drawing size. I record each bracket and weld by its number, with the readings and units, and mark it accept or reject. Rejected welds are marked clearly on the part and kept apart. The record is signed and dated and given to the supervisor, and the rejects are raised for repair by an approved method.
markingPoints: Prepares: current documents, good light, suitable gauges in good condition; welds cleaned
Checks for cracks first: any crack is a reject
Measures undercut depth and leg lengths at several points and compares them with the limits
Records each weld by number with readings, units and accept or reject; signs and dates the record
Marks and separates rejects and raises them for repair

essays.stem: Explain how you would use mill certificates to check a delivery of steel for a job that needs full traceability, and how you would keep that traceability through cutting and welding.
essays.modelAnswer: When the steel arrives I compare the delivery note with the order, then match each plate or length to its certificate. I read the heat number, grade and size marked on the steel and check that they agree with the certificate. On the certificate I check that the grade, chemical analysis and test results meet the specification, for example the minimum yield strength for S355. Any steel without a matching certificate, or with wrong or missing marks, is kept apart (quarantined) and reported, not used. The certificates are filed with the job. Before a plate is cut, the heat number is copied onto each part with a paint marker or a low-stress stamp, as the specification allows, so that every usable offcut keeps it too. A traceability record lists each part number against its heat number. During welding, the welder's identification and the consumable batch are added to the weld record. At handover, the file links every part to its certificate, its welds and its inspection.
markingPoints: Matches the heat number, grade and size on the steel to the certificate
Checks the certificate values meet the specification
Quarantines and reports steel that does not match
Copies heat numbers onto each part before cutting and keeps a traceability record
Records welder identification and consumable batch; the file links parts to certificates and inspections

essays.stem: A new welding machine arrives at the Centre. Explain how you would use its manual to get it ready for use safely, and how you would make sure the trainees use it correctly.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the whole manual before unpacking, starting with the safety section. I check the delivery against the parts list and look for damage from transport. From the installation section and the rating plate I note the supply voltage, the input current and the fuse or breaker size, and give these to the Centre's qualified electrician, who makes the supply connection and checks the earth. I place the machine where the manual allows: with space around it for cooling air, out of rain and dust, on a firm level base. I then follow the set-up section to fit the leads or torch, the work return cable and the gas, and check the controls against the manual's description. I make a test weld at the data sheet settings. For the trainees I write a short work instruction from the manual, brief them, show them the set-up and let each one do it while I watch. The manual is kept near the machine, and its maintenance tasks go on a checklist.
markingPoints: Reads the safety and installation sections; checks the parts list and for damage
Gives supply details from the manual and rating plate to a qualified electrician, who connects it and checks the earth
Sites the machine as the manual says (cooling space, dry, firm and level)
Sets up and tests the machine following the manual
Trains trainees with a work instruction, a demonstration and supervised practice; maintenance checklist

essays.stem: Explain how you would use a paint data sheet and the job specification to plan the painting of a set of steel gates for a house in Montego Bay.
essays.modelAnswer: First I read the specification for the paint system: the surface preparation, the primer and finish coats, and the dry film thickness of each coat. I check that the data sheet is for the product named. From the data sheet I note the surface preparation needed, the mixing ratio and pot life of any two-pack paint, the thinning allowed and the method of application. I note the conditions: the lowest and highest steel temperature, the humidity limit and the gap above the dew point, which matter in Jamaica's humid weather. I note the drying and overcoat times so that I can plan the order of coats over the days. I work out the wet film thickness needed for the dry film asked for, and how much paint to order from the spreading rate, with an allowance for loss. I read the SDS for PPE, ventilation, storage and fire safety. During the work I record the weather, the batch numbers and the film thickness readings.
markingPoints: Reads the specification for the paint system and checks the data sheet matches the product
Notes surface preparation, mixing, pot life, thinning and application method
Notes the conditions (temperature, humidity, dew point) and the overcoat times to plan the sequence
Works out the wet film thickness and the quantity of paint
Uses the SDS for PPE, ventilation and storage; records conditions, batches and film readings

essays.stem: Compare a national or international standard, a job specification, a welding procedure specification (WPS) and a maker's manual. For each, say who writes it, what it covers and how binding it is on a job.
essays.modelAnswer: A standard is written by a standards body, such as a national bureau or an international organisation, through a committee of experts. It sets general agreed rules, for example for weld quality or steel grades. It is binding on a job only when a contract or a law calls for it. A job specification is written by the client's engineer or designer for one job. It states what this job must meet and often names the standards that apply, so it is binding under the contract. A WPS is written by the fabricator and backed by a procedure test. It gives the welder the exact process, consumables, settings and joint details, and must be followed for every weld it covers. A maker's manual is written by the maker of a machine or product. It explains safe installation, use and care, and following it is needed for safety and to keep the warranty. If these documents disagree, I do not choose: I raise a written query.
markingPoints: Standard: by a standards body; general rules; binding when a contract or law calls for it
Specification: by the client's engineer for one job; binding under the contract; names the standards
WPS: by the fabricator, backed by a test; must be followed by the welders
Manual: by the maker; safe installation, use and care; needed for safety and the warranty
Disagreements are raised in writing, not decided alone

essays.stem: Part of a specification can be read in two different ways. Explain what you would do, from finding the problem to briefing the team on the answer.
essays.modelAnswer: I would not guess, or pick the easier meaning. First I read the whole section again, with the definitions and any notes, and check the drawings and other documents in case they make the meaning clear. If it is still unclear, I stop any work that depends on it and tell the supervisor. I then write a request for information to the engineer or client, quoting the document, its revision and the exact words, explaining the two possible meanings and, if it helps, proposing one. I log the query with its date. While we wait, the team carries on with work that is not affected. When the written answer comes back, I file it with the job documents, note it on the controlled copy or register so that others know, and brief the team on what it means for their work. If the answer changes the cost or the time, the supervisor raises a variation with the client.
markingPoints: Rereads the section, definitions and related documents first; does not guess
Stops the work that depends on it and tells the supervisor
Sends a written query quoting the document, revision and wording, and logs it
Carries on with unaffected work; files the written answer and updates the documents
Briefs the team; cost or time changes are raised as a variation

essays.stem: A MIG machine in the workshop is giving uneven wire feed and porous welds. Explain how you would lead the team in using the maker's manual to find and fix the faults, and what you would record.
essays.modelAnswer: I would stop welding and get the manual's fault-finding chart for wire feed and for porosity. We would treat the two faults separately, because they may have different causes. For the wire feed, with the machine switched off and isolated, we would check the causes in the order the chart gives: the contact tip size and wear, the liner for kinks or dirt, the drive rolls for the right size and groove, and the drive-roll pressure. For the porosity we would check that the cylinder valve is open and the flow is at the data sheet value, that hoses and joints are not leaking, that the nozzle is clean and that no fan is blowing the gas away. We change one thing at a time and make a test weld after each change, so that we know which change fixed it. Anything outside the user tasks in the manual, such as internal electrical parts, goes to the technician. In the machine log I record the faults, the causes found, the parts replaced, the test result and who did the work.
markingPoints: Uses the manual's fault-finding chart, treating each fault separately
Isolates the machine before checking inside the wire feeder
Checks causes in order, one change at a time, with a test weld after each
Leaves work outside the user tasks to a technician
Records faults, causes, parts, test result and name in the machine log

essays.stem: A new specification requires low-hydrogen electrodes for all structural welds, stored and handled as the maker's data sheet says. Explain how you would brief your team and check that they follow it.
essays.modelAnswer: I would first read the specification and the maker's data sheet, so that I know exactly what is required: which electrodes, the holding oven temperature, how long they may be out of the oven, how to re-dry them and how many times this is allowed. I would make sure the shop has what is needed, such as a working oven, heated quivers and a log sheet. Then I would hold a short briefing at the work area. I would explain what is changing and why: moisture in the coating adds hydrogen to the weld, which can cause cracking. I would show the oven, the log sheet and how to draw and return electrodes, and ask each member to explain the steps back to me. I would put a short instruction on the oven. To check that the team follows it, I would look at the oven log each day, check quivers during work and watch for electrodes left out on benches. I would record the briefing and correct any problem straight away.
markingPoints: Reads the specification and data sheet for the storage, exposure and re-drying rules
Makes sure the oven, quivers and log sheet are available
Briefs the team, explains why (hydrogen cracking) and checks their understanding
Posts a short instruction at the oven
Checks the oven log and quivers each day; records the briefing and corrects problems

practical1.title: Review a specification pack, check incoming steel and inspect sample welds against the acceptance limits
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a specification pack for a small steel job (for example a set of handrail posts): a short specification with acceptance limits, a drawing in two revisions, a WPS, two or three mill certificates, a paint data sheet and a document register. The pack has about five planted problems, such as an out-of-date revision, a size that differs between documents, or a plate whose heat number does not match its certificate. The assessor also gives the group 4–6 welded samples and the plates named on the certificates. As a group: (1) check every document against the register and against each other, and enter each problem on a query log with the action you propose and who should decide it; (2) check the plates against the certificates and record the result; (3) inspect the sample welds with gauges against the specification's acceptance limits, record every reading and mark each weld accept or reject; (4) write a one-page review report with a short summary and recommendations, signed by the group. Share the work so that each member leads one part and checks another member's part. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Specification pack from the assessor: specification, drawing (two revisions), WPS, mill certificates, paint data sheet and document register
Steel plates or offcuts marked with heat numbers, to match against the certificates
4–6 welded samples (fillet and butt welds) with a mix of good welds and visible defects
Fillet weld gauge, undercut or bridge cam gauge, steel rule, magnifier and torch
Query log, inspection record and report forms; paint marker
photos: The specification pack laid out with the document register
A plate's heat number shown beside its certificate
A gauge in use on each welded sample
The samples marked accept or reject
checklist: Checked each document's revision against the register and found the out-of-date one
Found conflicts between documents and logged them with a proposed action and who should decide
Matched plates to certificates by heat number, grade and size, and recorded the result
Used the gauges correctly and applied the specification's acceptance limits to each weld
Recorded readings with units and a clear accept or reject for each weld
Wrote their share of the report clearly and checked another member's part
Explained the reason for a decision when the assessor asked
safety: Wear safety glasses and safety boots in the workshop, as the Centre's rules require
Wear gloves when handling cut plates and samples: edges can be sharp
Do not grind, file or change the samples; inspect them as they are
Keep walkways clear of plates and paperwork

practical2.title: Set up, maintain and fault-find a MIG welding machine from its manual, and write a work instruction
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a MIG welding machine already connected to its supply by the Centre's electrician, its operator manual, a wire data sheet and a job card (for example a fillet weld on 6 mm mild steel). Before the session the assessor plants two or three simple faults that the manual's fault-finding chart covers, such as a wrong-size drive roll, a loose or wrong contact tip, or the gas cylinder valve closed. As a group: (1) read the manual's safety and set-up sections and carry out the pre-use checks; (2) with the machine switched off and unplugged or isolated, carry out two of the manual's user maintenance tasks, such as cleaning the drive rolls and replacing the contact tip; (3) use the fault-finding chart to find and correct each planted fault, one change at a time, making a test weld after each change and logging it; (4) set the machine from the data sheet, make a test weld and record the final settings; (5) write a one-page work instruction for trainees on setting up this machine. Each member leads one stage and checks another member's stage. Open only the covers the manual says the user may open, and only with the machine isolated. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: MIG welding machine, already connected by the Centre's electrician, with its operator manual
Data sheet for the 1.0 mm (or the Centre's) solid wire, and a spool of that wire
Shielding gas cylinder with regulator and flowmeter, chained upright
Spare contact tips and the correct drive rolls; cleaning brush
Pieces of 6 mm mild steel plate for test welds
Fault log, settings record and work instruction forms
Full welding PPE for each member
photos: The machine switched off and isolated before maintenance
The drive rolls cleaned and the new contact tip fitted
The fault log, showing each fault, cause and fix
The machine controls at the final settings
checklist: Isolated the machine before opening the wire feed area or doing maintenance
Found the right sections of the manual quickly and followed them
Did the user maintenance tasks as the manual describes
Used the fault-finding chart in order, one change at a time, testing and logging each
Set the machine from the data sheet and fine-tuned it on a test piece
Made a sound test weld while wearing full PPE
Wrote a clear, correct part of the work instruction
safety: Switch off and unplug or isolate the machine before any maintenance; never open covers the manual does not allow
Only a qualified electrician connects or repairs the supply
Keep the gas cylinder chained upright and close its valve when not in use
Weld only in a booth or behind screens, with good ventilation and full PPE
Treat test pieces and contact tips as hot: use pliers and mark hot work
